# bugs #3843: mcs51: Branching Range Exceeded for jumps across inline assembler lines with a semicolon directly after the mnemonic

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3843/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Apply the first patch and close. Decide separately on the second patch, which is for another cause of the message.
- Patch: [bugs-3843-1.patch](../../patches/bugs-3843-1.patch), commit [`374c0e5d9`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/374c0e5d92722271bd9f683a7689319a787f7628). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
- Patch: [bugs-3843-2.patch](../../patches/bugs-3843-2.patch), commit [`1ff879f0d`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/1ff879f0d97af0ada535c7086b795c2323e615e9). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.

## Finding

The ticket's file is `firmware/src/usrp2/usrp_main.c` of libusrp 3.4.10. With the ticket's
options, a compiler built from r15242, which is SDCC 4.5.0, gives the ticket's message. Line 1389
of `usrp_main.asm` is `jz 00140$`, and the label is 131 bytes before it. A compiler built from
r17158 compiles the file and fails the first test under Verification. SDCC 4.2.0 was not tested.

## Cause

`asmLineNodeFromLineNode` in `src/mcs51/main.c` computes the size of each assembler line, and
`pcDistance` in `src/SDCCpeeph.c` adds these sizes when a peephole rule asks whether a label is in
range of a short jump. After the mnemonic, the function returns without a size when the next
character is `;`, `:`, or `=`. That is correct for a label, an assignment, and a comment line. In
`nop; nop; nop;` the comment follows the mnemonic directly, so the line got size 0. The assembler
reads it as one `nop`. The firmware's `SYNCDELAY` macro is `__asm nop; nop; nop; __endasm`, and
four of these lines are between the `jz` and its label. The peephole optimizer counted no bytes
for them and replaced the long jump by a short one. The condition is from r3236 (2004), so 4.2.0
has it too.

The message has a second cause, which the ticket's file does not exercise. `labelJTInRange` in
`src/SDCCpeeph.c` decides whether the mcs51 rules 260.a to 260.m replace the `ljmp` instructions
of a jump table by `sjmp`. It compared the distance of each case label with one limit that
increases with the index of the table entry. That is right for a label after the table. A label
before the table is farther from later entries, so the limit was too high for it.

## Fix

With the first patch, which fixes the ticket, `asmLineNodeFromLineNode` returns at a semicolon
only when no mnemonic precedes it. With the second patch, `labelJTInRange` computes for a label
before the table the distance from the label to the end of the entry's `sjmp` in the replacement
and accepts at most 127 bytes. The check for labels after the table is not changed.

## Decision

The second patch is separable. It changes another file and has its own test, and the ticket's
file compiles without it. Its limit is 127 bytes, although `sjmp` allows 128 bytes backward from
the end of the instruction, because `labelInRange` and the other branch of `labelJTInRange` use
127 for both directions. A table with a case label exactly 128 bytes before the end of an entry's
jump keeps its `ljmp` instructions, 1 byte longer each. A limit of 128 was not tested.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3843.c` has a backward and a forward jump across 140 lines of
`nop; nop; nop;`. Without the first patch, the assembler reports the message for both jumps with
six sets of mcs51 options: the small, medium, large, and huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the
small and large models. With the patch, the test passes with these and on host, stm8, and z80.
The first patch was also applied to r15242, and that compiler compiles the ticket's file.

`support/regression/tests/bug-3843-2.c` has a case label 110 `nop` instructions before its jump
table. With the first patch alone it does not assemble with any of the six sets of options. With
both patches it passes with them and on host, stm8, and z80, and a table has `sjmp` when its label
is 127 bytes back and `ljmp` when the label is 128 or more bytes back. On r17176 with both
patches, the regression suite for these nine targets and the diagnostics suite have no failure.

## Related

- The entry local 0006 describes a third cause of this message on mcs51, peephole rule 257.c,
  which replaces `sjmp` by `ljmp` without a range check. The two patches of this ticket do not
  correct that cause, and the entry local 0006 has a patch for it.
- `src/ds390/main.c` and `src/hc08/main.c` have the same condition in their line parsers, as read
  from the source. Neither file is changed, and the two ports were not tested.
